name: Haiti
summary: Blue over red with the coat of arms on a white square: a royal palm topped by a liberty cap, with cannons, muskets and drums, and the motto 'L'Union fait la force'. Its origin is the French tricolour, with the white torn out by Jean-Jacques Dessalines in 1803.
origin: During the Haitian Revolution, on 18 May 1803 at the Congress of Arcahaie, Dessalines is said to have torn the white out of a French tricolour, symbolically rejecting the white colonists, and sewn the blue and red together; tradition credits Catherine Flon with the sewing.
Haiti became independent on 1 January 1804. The Duvalier dictatorship (1964–1986) used a black and red flag. After Jean-Claude Duvalier fled in 1986, the blue and red flag was restored.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The gens de couleur (mixed-race people), united with the Black population.

symbols.name: Weapons and drums
symbols.description: Cannons, muskets with bayonets, flags, a drum and cannonballs.

symbols.name: Motto
symbols.description: 'L'UNION FAIT LA FORCE' on a ribbon.

history.label: Blue and red flags
history.note: Horizontal and vertical versions at various times.

facts: Flag Day, 18 May, is one of Haiti's most important holidays.
At the 1936 Olympics, Liechtenstein discovered its flag was identical to Haiti's plain civil flag.
Haiti was the first nation founded by formerly enslaved people.
clues: Blue over red with a palm tree and liberty cap on a white square.
Created by tearing the white out of a colonial power's tricolour.
